# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 1

**1:1** The ancient records of the twelve tribes of Israel tell of a man named Joachim — a man of extraordinary wealth. Whenever he brought his offerings to the temple, he always gave twice the required amount, telling himself: "The surplus will benefit all the people, and my gift will bring forgiveness for everyone; this is how I will make things right before God."

**1:2** On one of the great feast days, when the people of Israel were streaming in to present their offerings, a man named Reuben blocked Joachim's way. "You have no right to present your offering before the others," he said bluntly. "You've never fathered a child in Israel."

**1:3** Joachim was devastated. He went to the genealogical archives and searched through the records of all twelve tribes, asking himself: "Am I truly the only man in Israel who has never had children?" He pored over the lists and found that every righteous man had indeed fathered offspring. Then he remembered Abraham — even Abraham, in his old age, had received the promised son Isaac from God.

**1:4** Heartbroken, Joachim slipped away without going home to his wife. He went out into the desert wilderness, set up his tent, and began a fast — forty days and forty nights. "I will not touch food or water," he told himself, "until God himself comes to me. Prayer will be the only thing that sustains me."
